commercial_incentive: Appears to be a counseling business's own channel, though no explicit sales pitch appears in this transcript
key_insights: Recommends a balanced list across three categories: reach (below-average GPA/scores for that school, often under ~20% acceptance), match (stats align, roughly 50-65% admit likelihood), and safety (stats comfortably above requirements, roughly 80-90% likelihood)

Cautions that even strong students can be denied at reach schools for reasons unrelated to merit, such as legal/residency status or financial need, so lists should stay realistic to avoid excess emotional weight on one school

Recommends evaluating five factors when building a list: location/campus environment, school size, major availability and program strength, cost/affordability including in-state vs out-of-state and aid eligibility, and campus culture
Advises visiting campuses when possible, citing cases of students who chose prestigious schools without visiting and later felt unhappy with the environment
Recommends an overall list of about 8-12 colleges, suggesting roughly 3-5 schools per reach/match/safety category as a working list, even though a student may apply to fewer
Suggests starting list-building as early as freshman year, since the list is flexible and can be revised as interests and stats develop
Recommends using resources like Naviance/Scoir and College Board data to research requirements and recent acceptance data when building the list
specific_numbers_or_facts: Reach schools defined as acceptance rate under ~20% (or under ~10% cited later) with below-average applicant stats
Match schools defined as roughly 50-65% admit likelihood for the applicant
Safety schools defined as roughly 80-90% admit likelihood
Recommended list size: about 8-12 colleges total, roughly 3-5 per category (up to 15 suggested as an evaluative pool)
Example given: NYU cited as having approximately 55,000+ students including grad programs
notable_or_distinctive: Standard reach/match/safety framework presented with specific percentage bands and a concrete worked example (Montclair as safety, Rutgers as match, Princeton as reach for an in-state NJ student).
reliability_notes: Percentage thresholds (20%, 50-65%, 80-90%) are presented as general rules of thumb without a cited data source; advice is generic and consistent with widely used counseling frameworks, not tied to a specific study.
